t.2.110.1: Thus addressed by Anasūyā, Vaidehī, who was herself free from envy, honored her words in return and softly began to speak.
t.2.110.2: It is no wonder in a noble lady that you speak to me thus; but this is known to me as well, that for a woman her husband is her guru.
t.2.110.3: Even if this husband of mine were devoid of good conduct, noble lady, still he would have to be served by me without wavering.
t.2.110.5: The very conduct that mighty Rāma maintains toward Kausalyā, he maintains toward the other wives of the king as well.
t.2.110.4: How much more, then, one who is praiseworthy for his virtues, compassionate, master of his senses, steadfast in his love, righteous of soul, devoted to his mother and dear to his father?
t.2.110.6: Even toward women whom the king has looked upon but once, the hero, devoted to the king and knowing dharma, sets aside pride and conducts himself as toward a mother.
t.2.110.7: Indeed, what my mother-in-law impressed upon me as I was setting out for this lonely forest, so fearsome, remains fixed in my heart.
t.2.110.8: And the counsel with which my mother instructed me long ago, at the time my hand was given in marriage before the sacred fire, that word too has been held fast by me.
t.2.110.9: But all of that has been made fresh again by your words, O you who walk in dharma: for a woman no austerity is ordained other than devoted service to her husband.
t.2.110.10: Sāvitrī, having devotedly served her husband, is honored in heaven; and you too, being of the same conduct, have won heaven through service to your husband.
t.2.110.12: And excellent women of this kind, firm in their vow of devotion to their husbands, are honoured in the world of the gods through their own meritorious deeds.
t.2.110.11: She too, the foremost of all women, is a goddess in heaven; and is Rohiṇī ever seen without the moon, even for a moment?
t.2.110.13: Then Anasūyā, delighted on hearing the words spoken by Sītā, kissed Maithilī on the head and spoke, gladdening her further.
t.2.110.14: Great ascetic power, won through manifold observances, is indeed mine. Relying on that strength, O Sītā of pure vows, I wish to gratify you with a boon.
t.2.110.15: "Your words, Maithilī, are fitting and proper, and I am pleased; tell me, what suitable thing may I do for you?" "It is already done," said Sītā to her who was endowed with the power of austerity.
t.2.110.16: Addressed thus by her, she who knew dharma became even more delighted: “Well then, Sītā, I shall make your joy bear fruit.”
t.2.110.17: O Vaidehī, here are this divine and excellent garland, this garment and these ornaments, along with costly body-paint and this fragrant unguent.
t.2.110.18: O Sītā, may this which I have given adorn your limbs; befitting you and never sullied, it will remain so forever.
t.2.110.20: Maithilī accepted the garment, the body ointment, the ornaments and likewise the garlands, an unsurpassed gift of affection.
t.2.110.19: O daughter of Janaka, with my limbs anointed with divine unguent, I shall adorn my husband, just as Śrī adorns the imperishable Viṣṇu.
t.2.110.21: And the illustrious Sītā, steadfast, having accepted that gift of affection, sat in attendance upon the ascetic woman rich in penance, her palms joined together in reverence.
t.2.110.22: Then Anasūyā, firm in her vows, began to ask Sītā, who sat beside her, to speak and tell some pleasing tale.
t.2.110.23: O Sītā, the story has reached my ears that you were won at a svayaṃvara by this illustrious Rāghava.
t.2.110.24: I wish to hear that story in detail, O Maithilī; you should tell it to me in its entirety, just as it was experienced.
t.2.110.25: Thus addressed, Sītā then said to that woman who walked in righteousness, "Listen," and told her that story.
t.2.110.26: The heroic lord of Mithilā, named Janaka, a knower of dharma, devoted to the dharma of the kṣatriyas, rules the earth with justice.
t.2.110.27: As he, plough in hand, was ploughing the circle of the field, I, it is said, rose up, splitting open the earth, and became the daughter of that king.
t.2.110.28: Seeing me with my whole body covered in dust, that lord of men, Janaka, who was intent on scattering handfuls of seed, was filled with wonder.
t.2.110.29: Being childless, he lovingly lifted me onto his lap himself, and saying, “This is my daughter,” he lavished his affection upon me.
t.2.110.30: And in the sky, it is said, a voice was uttered, incomparable and superhuman: “So it is, O lord of men; by dharma she is your daughter.”
t.2.110.31: Then my father, the righteous-souled lord of Mithilā, was overjoyed; that king of men, having obtained me, attained abundant prosperity.
t.2.110.33: But seeing that I had reached the age when union with a husband is fitting, my father, dejected, fell into anxious thought, like a man made poor by the loss of his wealth.
t.2.110.32: And I was given, as one longed for, by that doer of virtuous deeds to the eldest queen; and by her, full of tenderness, I was cherished out of a mother's love.
t.2.110.34: In this world, the father of a maiden, even if he be equal to Śakra on earth, suffers humiliation from people both equal and inferior to him.
t.2.110.36: Knowing me to be not born of a womb, that lord of the earth, though he pondered long, could not find a husband for me who was equal and suited to me.
t.2.110.35: Seeing that outrage so near at hand to himself, the king, sunk in an ocean of anxiety, could not reach the farther shore, like a man without a boat.
t.2.110.37: As that wise man pondered ceaselessly, this resolve arose in him: "I shall hold a svayaṃvara for my daughter."
t.2.110.39: That bow, which men could not move even with great effort because of its heaviness, the lords of men could not bend even in their dreams.
t.2.110.38: At that time, at his great sacrifice, the great-souled Varuṇa lovingly gave him an excellent bow and two quivers with inexhaustible arrows.
t.2.110.40: Having obtained that bow, my truth-speaking father first summoned the kings and then made a proclamation in the assembly of the lords of men.
t.2.110.41: The man who lifts up this bow and strings it, to him my daughter shall be wife; there is no doubt.
t.2.110.42: And having seen that most excellent of bows, like a mountain in its heaviness, the kings saluted it and went away, unable to lift it.
t.2.110.43: After a very long time, this Rāghava of great splendor, accompanied by Viśvāmitra, has come to see the sacrifice.
t.2.110.44: Rāma, of true valor, came together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, while the righteous-souled Viśvāmitra was greatly honored by my father.
t.2.110.45: There he spoke to my father about the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa: “These two sons of Daśaratha wish to see the bow.” Addressed thus by that brahmin, he had the bow brought forth.
t.2.110.46: In the mere space of a blink, that valiant one bent the bow, and, swiftly fixing the string upon it, the mighty hero drew it to the full.
t.2.110.47: As he drew it with great force, the bow broke in two in the middle, and its sound was terrible, like that of a falling thunderbolt.
t.2.110.48: Then and there, my father, true to his pledge, raised up an excellent vessel of water, and I was made ready to be given to Rāma.
t.2.110.49: But Rāghava did not then accept her as she was being given, for he did not know the wish of his father, the lord, the ruler of Ayodhyā.
t.2.110.50: Then, having invited my father-in-law, the aged King Daśaratha, my father gave me to Rāma, whose self is well known.
t.2.110.51: And my own younger sister, the virtuous and lovely Ūrmilā, was likewise given by my father himself to Lakṣmaṇa to be his wife.
t.2.110.52: Thus was I given to Rāma then, at that svayaṃvara, and I am devoted, in accordance with dharma, to my husband, the best among the valiant.
